name: chatos-browser-cdp
description: Operate managed Chromium sessions or an explicitly connected Chrome browser through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

interface.shortDescription: Full browser control through Chrome DevTools Protocol
interface.longDescription: Launch an isolated managed Chrome browser or connect to an explicitly paired existing Chrome session. Existing-Chrome mode also requires the Chatos Browser Bridge Chrome extension and one explicit first connection; later restarts reconnect automatically. Supports high-level browser automation and raw CDP commands with local permission enforcement.
defaultPrompt: Users describe browsing goals, not tool sequences; automatically open or reuse a Browser CDP session. The MCP process binds it internally, so never provide, request, copy, guess, or reconstruct browser_session_id in later tool arguments.
After navigation or page changes, inspect a fresh snapshot before interacting and use only current element refs.
Verify meaningful actions with a fresh snapshot or session-status read, and recover once from a timed-out navigation before reporting failure.

permissions.reason: Launch the installed Browser CDP stdio MCP executable.
Launch an isolated local Chrome or Chromium process.
Read page structure, accessibility snapshots and visible content.
Navigate, click, type, scroll and control browser tabs.
Connect to an explicitly paired existing Chrome browser through the Chatos Browser Bridge extension.
Inspect console, network, WebSocket and HAR activity.
Abort or mock explicitly selected network requests.
Upload user-selected files and expose downloaded files as managed artifacts.
Execute explicitly approved raw Chrome DevTools Protocol commands.
